subject: Post-call: Reserved inference fitmap, isolation priorities & MOP
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@heliomed.com>, Procurement <procurement@heliomed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Reserved inference fitmap, isolation priorities & MOP

Alex / team —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard, where we landed, and proposed next steps so we have alignment. I tried to keep this tight so Procurement can scan it quickly.

Key customer pain points / goals (as discussed):
- Latency-sensitive clinical inference: consistent p95 < 120ms for 512-token sequences (primary goal).
- Data isolation requirement for PHI workloads: VPC + tenant isolation across inference pools; must support separate KV caches per tenant and no cross-tenant persistence.
- Predictable cost and scaling: committed monthly capacity for predictable throughput during peak windows (8am–8pm ET), with burst capacity for overnight batch jobs.
- Auditability: requestable token-level logs, request tracing, and SOC2 evidence for the environment.

What Redwood proposes (high level):
- Reserved (dedicated) inference pool: x8 A100 (or equivalent) nodes in a single region; configured as an isolated pool for HelioMed PHI traffic.
- SLO targets: p95 generation latency target 120ms for 512 tokens; uptime SLA 99.95% for the dedicated pool.
- Operational playbook (MOP): canary rollout, pre-warm KV caches for top prefixes, and staged autoscale buckets for expected peak load.
- Security/compliance: VPC peering + KMS integration; we will provide SOC2/ISO artifacts and an optional audit window.

Open clarifying items / risks identified on the call:
1) Exact steady-state concurrency and expected RPS during peak periods (Alex — can you confirm target RPS and typical request size distribution?).
2) Procurement timeline & PO cadence (Procurement team — rough ETA for contract review + signature?).
3) Isolation topology: single isolated pool vs. per-environment pools (we recommended single-isolated pool with tenant-level KV partitions; Jordan to validate scalability implications).

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- Alex: share sample throughput profile (CSV) and one week of anonymized request traces — by EOD Jul 3.
- Jordan: schedule technical deep-dive (30–45m) to validate KV/cache behavior and quantization options — propose Wed/Thu this week.
- Neha: draft ops-runbook skeleton and initial SLA language for Procurement — deliver SLA draft by Jul 2.
- Irene: attach initial SLA draft + isolation topology diagram (attached) and send a commercial outline for committed capacity and burst policy — by Jul 1.

Attachments included: HLMD_SLA-draft-v1.pdf (working draft), isolation-topology-diagram.png

If that matches your understanding, please reply with any edits and confirm the data you’ll share. Thank you — excited to keep momentum.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

This message contains confidential information intended for HelioMed and Redwood sales stakeholders.
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@heliomed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@heliomed.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Reserved inference fitmap, isolation priorities & MOP

Irene — thank you for the concise recap. That aligns closely with our view. A few notes / answers to open items: 

1) Throughput: our target steady-state RPS during clinic hours is ~120 RPS for 1–2 token prompts (mostly short clinical queries), with spikes up to ~380 RPS during morning batch load when multiple clinics sync. Attached is a sample CSV of anonymized request timestamps and sizes (see separate upload).
2) Procurement: we can get a redline window scheduled next week. Procurement team estimates 2–3 weeks for contract review once we receive the initial SOW and pricing.
3) Isolation: single isolated pool with tenant-level KV partitions sounds preferable from our end — reduces inter-pool idle cost. Concern: cache eviction behavior during spikes.

Also: one more requirement surfaced — we need a support escalation path that guarantees a 1-hour P1 response for the first 6 months after go-live (we can discuss whether that becomes part of paid support).

Action: I will share the CSV and a short load breakdown by EOD Jul 3. Jordan, happy to take the technical deep-dive — Wed 09:00 PT works for me.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Rivera
Director, AI Engineering | HelioMed
alex.rivera@heliomed.com | +1 617-555-0198
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Reserved inference fitmap, isolation priorities & MOP

Forwarding Alex's confirmation —

Jordan here. Quick technical notes ahead of the Wed deep-dive:
- We should validate KV cache size per-tenant and ensure prefix pre-warm during morning spikes; suggest a warm-up job triggered 20 minutes before peak.
- For the p95 target at 512 tokens, quantization to int8 for the non-clinical fallback model could save ~30% GPU time; we'll show perf numbers on the call.
- Need to confirm whether HelioMed requires dedicated NVLink-only topology (for lower cross-GPU latency) or if standard fabric is fine. Alex, can you flag preferred topology?

I'll draft a short test matrix to run during POC to validate latency under synthetic spike conditions. Neha — can you prep the ops checklist and rollback steps?

-Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@heliomed.com>, Procurement <procurement@heliomed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: Reserved inference fitmap, isolation priorities & MOP

Appreciate the quick responses and the throughput numbers, Alex — that helps a lot. Confirming the mutually agreed next steps and dates so we can lock the calendar: 

Confirmed next steps / owners: 
- Alex: share anonymized trace + CSV (due EOD Jul 3) — will be used to size the reserved pool and refine autoscale buckets.
- Jordan: technical deep-dive on Wed Jul 2, 09:00 PT (calendar invite sent). Deliverable: test matrix + POC perf targets.
- Neha: SLA & ops-runbook draft (deliver Jul 2 COB). Will include support escalation (we'll propose 1-hour P1 response as an add-on in the SLA draft).
- Irene: commercial sketch (committed monthly GPU hours, burst policy, and price bands) + updated SLA draft attached (HLMD_SLA-draft-v1.pdf) — deliver Jul 1.

Commercial ask / tentative sizing (subject to traces): initial reserved configuration proposal: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (isolated pool) with the option to add 4 GPU burst nodes. Pricing / commitment bands will be in the commercial sketch.

Procurement note: for the contract, please expect an initial SOW + SLA + Data Processing Addendum. If Procurement can provide preferred contract language or redlines up front, we can accelerate the review.

Please reply if any of these are off. Otherwise we'll proceed against these dates.

Thanks again — looking forward to the technical call.

Best,
Irene
